The right-hand side has no expansion or loop risk. The one concern is the `Fintype` instance fixed in the statement. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested whether simp actually fails to match. findings.problem: This is a `@[simp↓]` lemma, but its left-hand side is a `Finset.univ` product over the subtype `{w // w.asIdeal.LiesOver v.asIdeal}`. The `Fintype` instance in that product is the scoped `Fintype.ofFinite` instance. Simp matches instance arguments of the pattern by unification, so it will probably only fire on products whose `Fintype` instance is syntactically `Fintype.ofFinite _`. A product elaborated with another instance, such as one from `Fintype.ofEquiv` or a `let _ : Fintype ..` binder, may not match. `Sum.finrank_adicCompletion` in Semilocal/Basic.lean builds such an instance with `Fintype.ofEquiv _ (liesOverEquivPrimesOver ..)`. Downstream code already needs ad-hoc workarounds. Ideles/Extension.lean introduces `let _ : Fintype {w : ..} := Fintype.ofFinite _` and uses an explicit `rw [← ...]`. Places/Extension.lean repeats the `attribute [local instance] Fintype.ofFinite in` line so its own `simp↓` lemma will match. The simp interface is therefore tied to one arbitrary instance choice.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma for an arbitrary instance: add `[Fintype {w : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L) // w.asIdeal.LiesOver v.asIdeal}]` to the hypotheses and delete `attribute [local instance] Fintype.ofFinite in`. The instance variable is then unified with whatever instance the goal contains. To keep the proof working, finish it with `Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum`. For `sum_finrank_adicCompletion_eq_finrank`, either make it instance-generic too or convert with `Subsingleton.elim` or `convert`. If an instance-generic version is unwanted, keep the current form and add a `Finite`-based `finprod` variant. A `finprod` statement does not depend on a `Fintype` instance, so simp can match it from any context.
findings.benefit: The simp lemma fires on products over this subtype however the `Fintype` instance was produced. Callers no longer need `Fintype.ofFinite` boilerplate, which now appears in at least two downstream files, just to make the rewrite apply. The result is a more reliable normal form for `∏ w ∣ v, ‖ι_w x‖`.
